newsitem.title: USA: Georgia voters approve school funding tax.
newsitem.headline: Georgia voters approve school funding tax.

text.p: Georgia voters approved a referendum allowing school systems to fund construction with sales taxes, state school officials said Wednesday.
Voter totals were not immediately available, "but we know it passed," said Jeff Chandler of the state school superintendent's office.

The one-cent local-option tax could be collected for up to five years, but would still have to be approved by local referendum before any school district could impose it. A subsequent referendum would be required to extend the tax beyond the five-year limit.

Georgia school districts have traditionally financed construction with long-term bond issues backed mainly by property taxes. The newly approved amendment would allow them to use the sales tax revenue to retire oustanding school bonds, so long as that purpose is spelled out in the local referendum enacting the tax.
